blocks.text: From 1925 Turkmenistan was one of the republics of the Soviet Union, the Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic. In 1991 the Union was coming apart. The republic's parliament, the Supreme Soviet, had already declared its sovereignty on 22 August 1990, and in March 1991 its voters took part in the all-Union referendum on keeping a renewed Soviet Union: by the official result, 98 percent of them were in favour.

After the failed coup attempt in Moscow in August 1991, most Soviet republics declared independence. Turkmenistan held a referendum on independence on 26 October 1991; by the official result, more than 94 percent of the voters said yes. The next day, 27 October 1991, the Supreme Soviet adopted a constitutional law on independence, and the state took the name Turkmenistan. Two months later, on 26 December 1991, the Soviet Union ceased to exist.
Independence Day, *Garaşsyzlyk baýramy*, was celebrated on 27 October for more than twenty-five years. A constitutional law of 2017 moved it, and since 2018 the holiday has been held on 27 September.

The second date came four years later. On 12 December 1995 the United Nations General Assembly adopted, without a vote, resolution 50/80 A, “Permanent neutrality of Turkmenistan”. It recognizes and supports the status of permanent neutrality that Turkmenistan had declared and confirmed in its own law, and calls on the member states to respect it, along with the country's independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity.

The General Assembly supported the status again in resolutions of 2015 and 2025, and in 2017 it proclaimed 12 December the International Day of Neutrality. In Turkmenistan the day is a public holiday, *Bitaraplyk baýramy*, Neutrality Day, and 2025 marked thirty years of the status.

The two key words are built the same way. *garaşsyz* means **independent** and *bitarap* means **neutral**; the suffix *-lyk* turns them into the nouns *garaşsyzlyk*, independence, and *bitaraplyk*, neutrality. You will meet *-lyk* properly in [A2 unit 12](a2-u12).

blocks.title: Dates with a year
blocks.text: A full date runs from the year down, with the ordinals of [A1 unit 11](a1-u11): *1991-nji ýylyň 27-nji oktýabry*, 27 October 1991, literally **of the year 1991, its 27th of October**. For **on** that day, add the locative after the possessive: *1991-nji ýylyň 27-nji oktýabrynda*.
With this unit's past tense, you can read this:

blocks.tk: 1991-nji ýylyň 26-njy oktýabrynda Türkmenistanda referendum boldy. Adamlar garaşsyzlyk üçin ses berdiler. 27-nji oktýabrda Türkmenistan garaşsyz döwlet boldy. 1995-nji ýylyň 12-nji dekabrynda BMG Türkmenistanyň bitaraplygyny ykrar etdi. Şonuň üçin 12-nji dekabr Bitaraplyk baýramy.
blocks.en: On 26 October 1991 a referendum was held in Turkmenistan. People voted for independence. On 27 October Turkmenistan became an independent state. On 12 December 1995 the UN recognized Turkmenistan's neutrality. That is why 12 December is Neutrality Day.

questions.q: When was the referendum on independence held?
questions.explain: The next day, 27 October, the Supreme Soviet adopted the law on independence.

questions.q: On what day has Independence Day been held since 2018?
questions.explain: It moved from 27 October to 27 September. 12 December is Neutrality Day.
